anchor.statement: Lemma 8.7. Suppose that the fixed slow base satisfies (8.24) on the reserved interior interval I m , with λ > 0 and |a( η )| ≥ a 0 > 0. There are three fixed azimuthal bump profiles and two fixed axial bump profiles supported in this interval with the following property. At each (Z, T), for arbitrary scalar targets (P, J θ , J z ), their physical rescalings have a unique linear combination ( ∆ v, γ d ) satisfying ∫︂ R 2∆ v dR = 0, ∫︂ R γ d dR = 0, ∫︂ (2V/R) ∆ v dR = −P, ∫︂ R 2 (G ∆ v + V γ d ) dR = −J θ , ∫︂ (2RG γ d − RV ∆ v) dR = −J z . (8.25) The target triple is normalized row by row as in (8.17). The resulting increments are independent of the angular and auxiliary variables and depend linearly on the targets. For every α , targets in S α give increments in M α , for every fixed coefficient derivative, with constants permitted to depend on the fixed λ . The azimuthal-potential realization (8.14) has ∆ γ = γ d exactly and ∆ β ∈ M α +1 . The two integral constraints are preserved exactly. When the targets are the current defects defined by Equations (8.12) and (8.15), the last three equations cancel the displayed contributions involving the fixed base.

correspondence.by: Christian Garry (drafted with Claude Code; second review by ChatGPT, checked)
correspondence.note: reserved_five_rows states that the bump increments solve the five rows of (8.25) on the actual reserved patch with the shaped amplitude, and five_rows_on_patch does so for V = C R^(−1−2λ), G = 0; matrix_det_ne_zero states that the bump power-moment matrix is nonsingular. Uniqueness within the bump spans requires reducing the five rows to these two moment matrices; the S_α → M_α bound (rank_update_meanClass, stated with a constant background coefficient B ≠ 0) must be transferred to the η-dependent shaped amplitude using inverse_kernel_jet_bound; exact ∆γ = γ_d and ∆β ∈ M_{α+1} come from actual_rank_stream_identities and rankIncrementState_bounds_of_components. That assembly is the reviewer's argument.
